newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends easier as yen bond prices slide.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends easier as yen bond prices slide.

text.p: The key September three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures contract closed easier on Thursday, weighed down by late falls in yen bond prices.
The Euroyen market started to factor in the impact of the yen's weakness against the dollar because bond yields and swap rates rose significantly in the afternoon, traders said.
The September settled at 99.29 after opening at 99.31. A total of 11,836 contracts changed hands.
The key contract rose as high as 99.32 by midday before falling to a session low of 99.29.

But the contract's fall was limited because there is a wide-spread belief in the market that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) is unlikely to change its low interest rate policy at least by the end of March, traders said.

"If the yen remains weak against the dollar, the key September may fall toward a psychological support point of 99.25," said a dealer at a long-term credit bank. "But the downside room should be limited because the BOJ is unlikely to raise its discount rate soon," he said.

Higher interest rates might stop the yen's further fall. But traders said the BOJ is unlikely to raise the discount rate from the current record low 0.5 percent because that would dampen the sluggish recovery of the economy.
"If the BOJ had to choose either a weak yen or weak stocks, it would prefer a weak yen because corporate earnings results are due in March," the dealer said.

A Reuters poll released today in which 28 economists responded showed that all but one expected the BOJ to leave its discount rate unchanged until the end of June, mainly because tax increases from April 1 will slow the economic recovery.
The December may take over benchmark status as of today if its turnover exceeds that of the September for the second day on Friday. The December's turnover was 17,784 contracts.
The BOJ conducted a neutral money market operation this morning, which was in line with expectations.
The key interbank overnight rate rose to 0.49 percent from Wednesday's 0.48. The short-end money rate was underpinned by banks' firm demand for monthly salary payments.
Key three-month certificates of deposit (CD) were not issued, but were offered at an unchanged 0.53 percent.
